translations.text: Jesus ✠ Christ. An encomium by our holy father, honored in every way, Apa Stephen, bishop of the city of Heracleopolis, which he delivered on the day of the holy martyr of Christ Jesus, Apa Elias, the sixteenth of Pasremhotp, as they celebrated his feast in his prayer house. In peace. Amen.
There are trees in distant lands. Even though we have not seen them face to face, by enjoying their fruits we come to know their beauty and sweetness.

For such are the victorious martyrs who have appeared in every city and region. Even though we did not go with them to the courtroom or witness the struggle they endured for Christ, through the abundance of gifts found in their prayer houses we come to know their greatness and their honor before the Lord. Truly, such is our chosen crown-bearer, the honored champion, Saint Elias, who is the reason for your devout gathering today. O champion Elias, who shines in both name and virtue, I see the holy words of our Savior fulfilled in you: “Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.”
It is.
But.
Truly, such is our chosen crown-bearer, the honored champion, Saint Elias, who is the reason for your devout gathering today.
O champion Elias, who shines in both name and virtue.
I see the holy words of our Savior fulfilled in you: “Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.”
But Christ said this about all the righteous.
Saint Elias himself became like the sun in his name, his virtue, and his light, through the designation of his name.
For the meaning of Elias, according to the Greek language, is “the sun.”
First, then, the name came together with his birth in the flesh.
Afterward his [?] became apparent, confirming the name.
[?] the name of this saint, then; honor him in keeping with his praise, as it is written in the Psalms. But the visible sun has an end to its light.
But the visible sun has an end to its light.
The light of the martyrs, however, is imperishable.
The sun sets, and then rises again.
The victorious martyrs do indeed set in their bodies through their death.
But they will come with the Lord [?] in glory, with the wreath of their sufferings preserved for them.
But let us turn to the account of the one for whose commemoration we have gathered today: Saint Elias, who skillfully directed his military service.
Elias is truly the general of Christ the King and the physician of everyone who is sick.
He was not a laborer among those who work the land, nor did he eat his bread by the sweat of his face.
Nor.
Nor did he live in poverty, so that you could not say that the hardship of poverty forced him to run into this arena of martyrdom.
Rather, he was a nobleman among those of high rank.
He was rich in visible things.
He was wealthy in the gifts of Christ.
He was one who fought all the more against visible enemies.
He is all the more victorious over the hidden evil adversaries.
He is close to the king of this world.
And he is a companion of the king of heaven and earth, Jesus Christ.
He was assigned to military service in the earthly regiment.
He too was assigned to the heavenly fold through the prize of confessing his faith.
He was [?]
But now he has become a healer of those who are near him and those who are far away.
The arena of your martyrdom is truly beautiful, O noble one.
Your crown does not fade.
The fruits of your righteousness are beyond counting.
To whom shall I compare you in holiness, O Saint Elijah?
I will compare you to the one who bears the same name as you, Elijah,
who was taken up by horses and chariots of fire,
who shut the sky and opened it again by the word of his mouth.
For that Elijah was the one who fasted for forty days and forty nights.
O such a great miracle-worker! After he burned the two captains of fifty and their hundred soldiers,
and after he slaughtered the priests of Baal, four hundred in number,
[?] he fled from the threat of a prostitute.
You too, O bearer of victory, bearer of the prize, bearer of God, bearer of the Spirit, and bearer of the crown of the new covenant—the honored martyr, the faithful noble one—
The honored martyr.
The faithful noble one.
The unconquerable athlete.
The victorious contestant.
Saint Elijah, you stood firm before the threats of kings.
You trampled upon the power of fire.
You became strong in battle against your enemies.
I will compare you to the wise Daniel.
He, for his part, stood against the kings of the Chaldeans.
But you too, O honored athlete,
He despised the commands of Darius and Cyrus.
you too, O bearer of Christ’s crown, despised the idol worshipers.
They threw Daniel into the lions’ den because he did not obey the decree of the Persians and the Medes.
But you too, O righteous one, did not endure only the ordeal of the wild beasts because of your confession of Christ.
Rather, you became strong in many struggles. I will compare you to the beloved learned physician, Luke the evangelist.
I will
You became like him in your following of Christ and your martyrdom for him.
I will therefore portray for you the story of Saint Elias, or rather the grace that came to him from the Lord.
Shall I speak of his struggle for God?
Or rather, of the help of the Most High that helped you?
Shall I speak of the tyrant’s anger and madness, or of this holy martyr’s endurance?
He was like sheep among wolves.
He was like lilies among thorns.
He shone among those in the darkness of the deception of idols. Those people lived in luxury, but the brave man was restrained by God.
The noble man, for his part, was being guided by God.
They worshiped what their hands had made, but Saint Elias worshiped the Creator alone, who is God.
And the ruler of this world, who rules those in darkness, was again urging him toward the things of darkness.
But the brave martyr’s citizenship was in heaven.
Now, then, consider the splendid theater filled with grace:
a single, all-holy man standing in the midst of God.
Are the people among the angels and the demons?
Those on earth were forcing him to sacrifice to earthly things.
But the King of heaven, Christ, was strengthening his brave man for the struggle.
“So will you not offer sacrifice, Elijah?” “No,” he said.
But the holy martyr said, “I am a physician, treating others.
And how could I tolerate letting my soul become sick through idol worship?
I am a soldier in the army on earth, but I do not want to be separated from the armies of the angels.
I am a citizen of the city on earth, but from today onward I will choose for myself the heavenly Jerusalem, the city of the [?] Holy One.”
What, then, will the powers of darkness do now?
What will the king who fights against God do?
He flattered.
He threatened.
He pleaded.
He became angry.
And, to put it briefly:
The rains came down.
The rain came upon them. The winds blew.
They blew.
They battered this saint’s resolve, but they could not shake him, because he was built upon the immovable rock, Christ. Then, since the first ordeal had ended,
Then, since the first ordeal had ended,
They called the athlete and fighter for the truth into the contest.
Again, there were extremely severe sufferings.
Again, confiscations and many instruments of torture.
Again, the [?] of the executioners.
Again, from one power to another power.
From one kingdom to another nation.
From one tribunal to another tribunal.
From many sufferings into great afflictions.
For the weapons of his warfare are not fleshly, but are powers belonging to God.
He showed himself to be following Christ, who stood before the high priest, Herod, and Pilate.
For the wise say:
As for the holy martyr Saint Elias, he distinguished himself in the first ordeal, the second, and the third.
Therefore his crowns [?] in splendor in heaven and on earth. He passed through fire and water, but the psalmist’s places of rest are reserved for him.
He passed through fire and water, but the psalmist’s places of rest are reserved for him.
They hung him on a tree, but it is enough for the disciple to become like his teacher, who was crucified for us.
He renounced his [?], their desire, and destructive pleasure.
But the banquet of the kingdom of heaven is prepared for him.
He left behind these temporary honors, but the everlasting good things are his.
He turned his face away from the kings of the earth.
But his is the vision of the light of the holy Trinity, one in essence.
They cut off his head with the sword, but he went to his true head, Christ. He renounced the king’s armor, but became like David, who cast Saul’s armor off himself.
It was women who came out to meet that man, dancing to celebrate his victory over the Philistine.
But for this brave man, it is angels who award him the prize, because he has defeated the father of all the Philistines, namely the devil.
You are blessed now, O victorious athlete.
Glorious is your victory, O you who entered many contests because of your love for God.
And the Lord will crown you with the crown of righteousness.
So let no one now disbelieve when hearing of all the sufferings that this victorious martyr endured for Christ.
For great is the abundance of healings that take place in large numbers at his shrine.
For these spread over everyone, almost like the shining rays of the sun.
What, then, are these? The healing of those who suffer;
the casting out of demons;
those who have approached the gates of death—such people he brings back to life again through the intercessions he makes for us before the Lord Jesus.
For he knows how to treat those suffering from dropsy through the skill of his medical practice, without payment.
He knows how to treat those who suffer, removing the [?] in their limbs.
In short, he heals everyone. This saint receives grace from God, who gives him what he asks for. He fulfills the request of each person who comes to his holy martyr’s shrine.
He fulfills the request of each person who comes to his holy martyr’s shrine.
You have seen that the one we have is a living protector [?], fighting on our behalf against a hidden enemy.
And he also heals our bodies.
For the day of his departure also suits these difficult circumstances.
For wise physicians commonly say about this month, Paremhat, that it is a month that naturally produces illness.
Because it is during this month that the trees begin to bud.
For God went down to Egypt at that time to bring the children of Israel out from among them through signs and wonders.
Also, during this month, the alternating periods of day and night become equal to one another.
Therefore, fittingly,
so that his holy prayers may be joined [?] with everyone who is sick in soul and body.
I have set these things before you, beloved, concerning the struggle of this noble martyr, Saint Elias.
Now, my beloved, I wish to speak a solemn word concerning the holy brothers whose bones have come to his resting place.
For it is something good.
The wise Solomon also said, “There are three that walk well.”
Therefore, the Lord fittingly arranged matters in this way, so that the bones of these three saints would rest beside one another.
So that the Holy Trinity, for whose sake they struggled, might be glorified through the naming of these three saints.
Now you, devout people, children of grace, who wish to run well and gain the kingdom of Christ our God: be diligent in coming to this place today, and also day after day.
But let no one seek only the healing of his body while we neglect the sins of our souls.

Look at the sufferings the martyrs endured: they were crowded into prisons, lying naked, their blood dripping onto the ground, hungry and thirsty, their bodies covered with wounds. Yet they did not give up, but pleaded with God night and day. Oh, what a great disgrace! We sleep with our hearts slack, and we do not concern ourselves [?] with the sufferings the holy one endured until they became worthy of life. Above all, the Lord of the saints, Jesus, spent a night keeping watch in prayer—not for himself, certainly not, but for us, wretched as we are, so that he might teach us the way to escape the snares of the evil one. See how empty everything in this world is! What benefit do we gain from celebrating the martyrs who struggled against sin to the point of death because of their faith in the Son of God?
Oh, what a great disgrace! We sleep with our hearts slack, and we do not concern ourselves [?] with the sufferings the holy one endured until they became worthy of life.

Above all, the Lord of the saints, Jesus, spent a night keeping watch in prayer—not for himself, certainly not, but for us, wretched as we are, so that he might teach us the way to escape the snares of the evil one.
See how empty everything in this world is!
What benefit do we gain from celebrating the martyrs who struggled against sin to the point of death because of their faith in the Son of God?
Yet we ourselves are full of passions of every kind and sins of many sorts, and we have not repented before the inspector [?] comes for us.

In a little while, the true farmer will come with terror [?] and examine his palm tree to see what kind it is. He may find that there is no substance inside it—that is, deeds filled with every virtue—but only the appearance of a shell, which is hypocrisy.
He may find that there is no substance inside it—that is, deeds filled with every virtue—but only the appearance of a shell, which is hypocrisy.
The name we bear and our rank are one thing, while the deeds we do in secret are another.
As it is written, “The things they do in secret are shameful even to speak about.”
Woe to the person who gives Satan room to dwell in him through the desire for impurity, because he did not let relief reach him while he was alive.
And if he dies before he repents, he will be in the place of eternal [?], where he will not be found or visited. Look, [?] said to his disciples when he was going to send them out to preach:
Look.
Luke the evangelist said, “He gave them authority to cast out unclean spirits and to heal every sickness and every infirmity.”
The person who casts the unclean spirits out of himself—that is, impure thoughts—heals his soul and his body.

O human being, cast these passions out of your soul—these desires for excess—and you will be rescued from the sleepless worm in the underworld. Drive away from yourself the desires of the flesh that oppose the spirit, and you will not be thrown out of the heavenly dwellings.
Drive away from yourself the desires of the flesh that fight against the spirit, and you will not be cast out of the dwellings of the heavenly beings.
Do not let our honoring the martyrs consist only of entering their shrine.
Instead, let us imitate their steadfastness. Let us hold fast to their endurance.
Let

Let us strive to match their love for God. They conquered the world and its desires of every kind. We, for our part, must not let the world and its wishes conquer us. They despised the threat of torture.
We
Those people gained fellowship with the heavens for themselves.
We, for our part, should establish our citizenship in that place.
For this is how we will become companions.
And if we do not attain martyrdom like Saint Elijah, let us nevertheless live in righteousness like the brothers who are beside him.
But

This other matter also belongs to the wisdom of God: he arranged for the bones of these ascetics to be beside those of the martyr, so that their story would encourage everyone to repent. If you live in a time of persecution, look at the one who conquered amid persecutions, Saint Elijah. Again, if you live without persecution, look at those who distinguished themselves through their way of life and their ascetic discipline. For the ascetic life is preparatory training, and it is no less demanding than the life of the martyrs. Therefore, since this is the case, I will bring you the wise apostle as an advocate for this matter, when he recounted to us the faith of each of the saints.
If you live in a time of persecution, look at the one who conquered amid persecutions, Saint Elijah. Again, if you live without persecution,
Again
And
Therefore
When he recounted to us the faith of each of the saints,

and when he brought forward Gideon, Barak, Samson, David, and Samuel, he set forth those who had conquered in the arena of martyrdom and joined the monastic life to them, saying this: “They wandered in deserts and mountains, in caves and holes in the earth, in need, afflicted, and suffering—people of whom the world was not worthy.”
They wander in deserts and mountains, in caves and holes in the earth, suffering deprivation, oppression, and hardship. These are people of whom the world is not worthy.
Finally, he crowned them all with the name of martyrdom, saying, “Therefore, since we have this multitude of witnesses set before us, let us run with endurance in the contest set before us.”
You see that the monastic life is the sister of martyrdom for anyone who practices it without hypocrisy or a cloak of falsehood.
For Christ himself has given us a model of these two struggles in his own person.
For he defeated the devil when he withdrew into the wilderness.

And again, he established the salvation of the whole inhabited world through the victory of his cross. To those in the wilderness he gave victory by becoming their leader in this. And again, for those who entered the arena of martyrdom, he became a crown.
Again.
As for us too, my brothers, let us follow the Lord and what belongs to the Lord. Let us confess the Lord along with the holy martyrs.
Let [?]
Let us be holy for him, like those who purified themselves for him through ascetic discipline. Let us guard our faith like the holy martyrs.
Let [?]
Let us be [?] in the love of our spirit.
For even if we will not shine like the sun, let us at least be seen among the ranks of the stars.

What I mean is this: even if we cannot reach the greatness of the martyrs’ struggles, let us at least be found in the company of the faithful. Even if we will not love God as he loved us, let us love one another in our own way.
But.
Even if.
And even if we have nothing to give him, comfort him with your words. Strengthen him with the promise of the kingdom of heaven.
Tell him the fitting words of the apostle: “The sufferings of this present time are not worthy of the glory that will be revealed to us.”
For poverty is martyrdom for anyone who bears it with gratitude.
For this is what Christ, the life of us all, said: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.”
And those who were persecuted because of righteousness, who will be called children of God, are the martyrs.
As for us too, my beloved, let us love our neighbors as the martyrs loved God and poured out their blood for him, so that we may find mercy on the day when we run to him.
May the Lord bless you all, from the least to the greatest among you, and awaken you from this negligence.

Be sober and watchful, for the adversary, the devil, walks in darkness night and day, unseen by us, seeking to devour our souls. I beg you all: let each person examine his life—what he has done and what he lacks. If he has sinned, let him repent of what he has done. And I trust in God and in the prayers of the holy martyr, Saint Elijah, that he will forgive him.
I beg.
If

Do not let us keep putting off one day after another, so that the messenger of death overtakes us and finds us unprepared, and we become afraid and curse the day on which we were first born. For the time has passed out of our hands, and the boat has been pulled to shore. Whatever is found inside it, whether good or bad, is what it has brought.
the time has passed out of our hands and they have shut [?] your door, whoever is found inside it, whether good or bad, is the one who has passed on.
It has passed. It is good for us to repent before they shut the door of repentance against us.
May our God, Christ Jesus, the Lord of heaven and earth, place his peace upon us and drive the devil and his demons away from us.
To him belong glory, honor, and worship, together with his good Father and the Holy Spirit—the perfect Trinity in unity, and the unity in a Trinity of one substance—forever and ever. Amen.
Jesus ✠ Christ. This is the martyrdom of the holy martyr of Christ, Apa Elijah, who completed his honorable struggle together with his companions on the sixteenth of Paremhat. In peace. Amen.

Now it happened that, when the apostles completed their proclamation according to the command of our Savior Jesus, they established the church fully, from the places where the sun rises to the places where it sets, so that the fragrance of their offering spread [?] the heavens, their hearts being upright in the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ.
And the name of God was glorified, and Mastema was put to shame.
The glory of the church appeared, but the idols delayed it until two hundred and forty-six years had passed since the ascension of our Savior Jesus Christ the Lord.

The whole world shared one faith, worshiping one God, Jesus Christ, together with his good Father and the Holy Spirit, forever and ever. Amen. Now it happened after this great [?], this long period during which the world had not sinned through idol worship,
Now it happened
and when Mastema realized that he and those who belonged to him had been put to shame,

he consulted with those who belonged to him, saying, “What shall we do [?] to draw the world to me again? Otherwise, they will not listen to me.” He devised a scheme of this kind so that he could make the world turn away as it had before. Likewise, it is necessary for the martyrs to receive crowns.

He deliberated within himself, saying, “I will enter the hearts of the great kings who rule the world and change their hearts. I will make them abandon the God of heaven and worship idols, shed blood, and [?] engage in deeds, struggling for nothing.”

These are the names of the kings who ruled at that time, each in his own country: 1. Liberianus, who was king over Iconia [?]. 2. Nicomedes, who was king over Persia. 3. Eutychodorus, who was king over Media. Diocletian, who was king over the Romans. Herodian, who was king over India.
When the devil deceived them, they abandoned the God of heaven, worshiped idols, and shed the blood of all the Christians, each in his own country.
Now there was a man named Soterichus, who served as Caesar under Herodian, the king of India.

When he saw that all the Christians were being mistreated because of the holy name of our Lord Jesus Christ, and also saw great miracles that had taken place through them, he too withdrew from the idols and believed in the true God, Christ Jesus.
And the holy Soterichus began to oppose the king.
He sent orders tyrannically and released all the Christians who were imprisoned.
When King Herodian heard this, he became extremely angry. He sent urgently and had Soterichus brought to him.

When he arrived, the king said to him, “Soterichus, what is this insolence you have committed in my kingdom? You have defied my command concerning what is proper for the gods, even though you rank next to me in my kingdom.” Soterichus answered, “From now on, may I never submit to a king of this world! Instead, I will cling to the feet of the true king, Christ Jesus, whose kingdom neither passes away nor dissolves. Now, king, stop troubling me. I will not worship your abominable gods, nor will I abandon my king, Jesus.”
Soterichus answered, “From now on, I will never submit to a king of this world. Instead, I will cling to the feet of the true King, Jesus Christ, whose kingdom never passes away or comes to an end.”
“Now then, O king—”
When he said these things, the king became very angry and ordered him to be bound.
When his soldiers saw him bound, they cried out, “Our lord, give the order, and we will release you and rescue you from the king’s hands.”
They said to them, “No, because it is the will of my Lord Jesus that I should die for his holy name.”
“Our Lord Jesus did not want war, but peace.”
“I too seek it. This belongs to you.”
They all cried out, “We are ready to do what you have said with joy.”
On that day, five commanders of a thousand were under his command, together with their multitude of soldiers.
And they came to the king with one purpose, saying, “We are all Christians. Whatever death our lord Soterichus is going to die, we too will die.”
When the king heard them, he became very angry—or rather, he was deeply disturbed.
He ordered them to be put aboard boats and taken out to the open sea. They cut off their heads and threw their bodies into the sea, while Saint Soterichus stood over them praying.
He looked and saw their souls like white doves ascending to heaven.
He too stretched out his head, and they cut it off.
Their total number was four hundred and fifty-six, together with the other five commanders of a thousand. They all completed their lives on a single day, the ninth of Tobe, in peace. Amen.
Listen now, my brothers, and I will tell you that God does not forget those who put their trust in him. Instead, he helps them and gives them strength.

When Saint Soterichus was martyred, there was a soldier in the palace who was thirty-three years old. His name was Elijah. He was handsome in appearance, vigorous in strength, and accomplished in every good work.
There was [?].
This man was a physician who attended the king at all times because of the cures he performed. Whenever an illness struck the king or his officials, he was the one who treated them.
For this reason, everyone in the palace loved him, from the least to the greatest.
Saint Elijah reflected every day on Saint Soterichus.
He would make his request, saying, “When I am worthy, reveal yourself to me so that I may see your face again.”
“As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I too will die the death that you died.”
When he fell asleep while reflecting on these things, a voice came to him: “Elijah, Elijah!”
He said, “Here I am, lord. Who are you who are calling me?”
Saint Elijah thought that an illness had struck the king and that he had sent for him to treat him.

The voice came to him a second time: “My chosen one, Elijah, I am not a king of the kind you are thinking of, who needs a physician to treat him. Open your eyes and recognize who I am. I am Jesus, the golden fragrance in the Father’s embrace.”
I
I am Jesus, the sweet fragrance of the true vine of the good Father.
I am Jesus, the guardian of the water of the [?] pool.
I am Jesus, the unbreakable bond of the ages.
“I am Jesus, who helps everyone who believes in him with all their heart.”
When Saint Elijah heard these things, he raised his eyes and saw Jesus seated above on the chariots of the cherubim.
Michael the archangel was on his right, and Saint Soterichus was on his left. He was wearing a glorious garment that no king of this world could wear.

When Saint Elijah saw these things, he fell down before the Lord, saying, “Forgive me, my Lord, for I am a sinful man. But I know, my Lord, that you grant repentance to the sinner when he turns back and repents. Therefore I beg you, my Lord Jesus Christ, who forgives all sinners: forgive me too for all the sins I committed while I did not know you.”
“Therefore I beg you, my Lord Jesus Christ, who forgives all sinners: forgive me too for all the sins I committed while I did not know you.”
Immediately Jesus raised him up, saying to him, “Rise, my chosen Elijah. I
am Jesus, who helps you. Truly I tell you, I will grant you my kingdom.

For I know that you will endure much suffering for my name. But do not be afraid. They will not be able to overpower you, because I am with you wherever they take you, strengthening you until you complete your struggle.

When the king sends for you tomorrow, do not go to him according to your [?]. He will send for you a second time, and they will compel you until they bring you to him. He will rebuke you, saying, ‘Why, when I sent for you, did you not come to me quickly?’ Answer him without any fear, with the holy words that I will put into your mouth.
He will rebuke you, saying, ‘Why did I send for you
Answer
But I am with you, and I will fill you with the Holy Spirit, strengthening you until my name is glorified through you.
So rise now and come greet your companion Soterichus, whom you asked to see.”
When the Savior had said these things to him, he gave him peace and went up to heaven in glory.
Likewise, a strong fragrance spread through the bedroom where Saint Elijah was sleeping.
When morning came, Saint Elijah did not go to the king’s palace.
Then the king sent for him. The messengers said to him, “The king is calling you, Elijah.
Why have you not come to the palace today?”
The saint said to them, “Go and tell the king, ‘Elijah, the servant of Jesus Christ, says: From this moment on, I will not submit to you, for it is not right for the living to
submit to the dead. Rather, the dead person submits to the living one, so that he too may live through him.’”
When the messengers heard these things from Saint Elijah, they reported these words to the king.
When the king heard these things, he became extremely angry and sent a military commander after him to have him brought to him against his will.
And when they brought him to him,
the king said to him, “Elijah, I love you very much. Why have you been so insolent and treated me with such contempt?”
Saint Elijah said to him, “All the gods of the nations are silver and gold.”
“Look, then, king: you have shown that you are a murderer, since you worship dead gods.”

“My God, Jesus Christ, is a living God, and everyone who lives and believes in him will live in him. It is written this way: ‘Just as my Father lives, and I too live because of my Father, you too will live because of me.’” When the king heard these things, he said, “Elijah, obey me and worship my gods, so that you may escape great and terrible tortures.”
This way: “Just as my Father lives, and I too live because of my Father, you too will live because of me.”
When the king heard these things,
“Do you want to die the bitter death of Soterichus?”
The saint said to him, “King, the death of Soterichus is not a bitter death. Rather, it is especially honorable,”
“because it is written this way: ‘The death of the Lord’s holy one is precious in his sight.’”
The king said to him, “Elijah, beloved one, do not make me hate you for nothing.”
But Saint Elijah began to put the king’s gods to shame.
He said, “King, since you have pressured me so much, I too do not want to distress you.”
“But I want you not to let anyone enter the temple until I have finished offering a sacrifice to your gods.”
The king ordered Saint Elijah to go inside.
Then the saint took an axe with him, concealed inside his clothes.

And when he saw the idols standing on their pedestals, he rushed at them with great power from God. He knocked them down from their pedestals with the axe in his hand. He cut their heads off their bodies, and the angel of the Lord suspended their bodies in the air in the middle of the temple.
The angel of the Lord suspended their bodies in the air in the middle of the temple.
Their heads lay at the foot of their pedestals.
Saint Elijah came outside and said to the king, “King, show me your gods.”
“For I went into the temple, but I did not find the gods there to worship them.”
“For it is written in the Gospel: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him alone.’”
When the king heard these things, he got up quickly and went into the temple. He saw nothing except the heads lying at the foot of their pedestals.
He ordered the priests to be brought to him and asked them, “Where are the gods we worship?”
They were afraid and could not find anything to say. Instead, they wanted to deceive the king.
They said to the king, “Our lord the king, live forever! Our gods fled from us, saying, ‘Some enemies of the king want to rise against him. We will go and win the war, then return to you.’”
When Saint Elijah heard this, he rejoiced greatly and laughed, saying, “So your gods forgot to take their heads with them when they went to war!”

When the king heard this, he was deeply ashamed. Indeed, he became extremely angry with the priests and said, “You ridiculous wretches who deserve destruction! Do gods go to war without heads on them?”
He said, “You ridiculous wretches who deserve destruction! Do gods go to war without heads on them?”

While the king was saying this, a voice came from the body of an idol suspended in the air inside the temple, saying, “King Herodianus, do not believe these priests who deceive you by saying, ‘We went to war to save you.’ We are not gods capable of winning a war.
We are not gods capable of winning a war.

For look, we are suspended in midair by the gods of Saint Elijah, and we have been unable to save ourselves [?], much less save you too. We beg you, king, to ask Saint Elijah to lower us, so that we do not fall.”
We beg you, king.
The king turned to Saint Elias and said to him, “Elias, I know that nothing is impossible for you, and when you are in the palace, you cure every illness without difficulty.”
“Likewise, I ask you to heal the gods and not leave them hanging, and to make their heads attach to their bodies again.”
Saint Elias said to the king, “Do human beings heal the gods, or do the gods heal human beings?”
The king said to him, “Truly, God heals human beings.”
Saint Elias said, “Truly, you have judged correctly.”
“Why, then, are you forcing me to heal these gods of yours, which you say are gods?
If they are gods, let them heal themselves.”
“But since you have asked me, king, to lower them and stop them from hanging in the air, I will not disappoint you.”
Then Saint Elijah raised his eyes to heaven and prayed,
saying, “Hear me, Jesus, the ear that hears, the eye that sees.”
Immediately the idols fell to the ground and were crushed. They became like chaff, together with their other heads that were lying on the ground.
Afterward a strong wind blew and scattered the chaff of the idols that had been broken on the ground.
When the king saw what had happened, he said to the saint, “Elijah, is this the favor you have done for me? I asked you for a favor, but you have made my gods like chaff before the wind!”
The saint said to the king, “It is written, ‘The ungodly person is like chaff that the wind blows away from the face of the earth.’”
“But you yourself, O king, if you continue to be ungodly—”
When the king heard this, he became extremely angry.
He ordered them to imprison him until the next day.
Saint Elijah spent the entire night praying to God.
As for the king, while he was sleeping that night, the devil came in to him in the form of a huge black dragon, with [?]. He was extremely terrifying.
When the king saw him, he was alarmed and cried out, “Who are you, whom I see in this shape and this terrifying form?” The dragon answered, “I am the devil, the enemy of the Christians.”
The dragon answered, “I am the devil, the enemy of the Christians.”

“Why did you let Elijah, this Christian sorcerer, destroy your gods? Do you want to become a Christian yourself and become my enemy? If so, I will punish you severely. Look, you can see how terrifying I am!”

The king was extremely alarmed, for the dragon’s eyes were shooting out fire. The king said to him, “My lord, whatever you tell me, I will do. Only do not destroy me!” The devil said to him, “If you will obey me, when you get up early tomorrow, have gods of gold made for you in place of these stone ones that Elijah destroyed.”

The king said to him, “My lord, whatever you tell me, I will do. Only do not destroy me.” The devil said to him, “If you will obey me, when you get up early tomorrow, have gods made for you out of gold.”
He said:
“And force him, too, to worship them. If he disobeys you, torture him even more.”

When the dragon had said these things, he bewildered the king’s mind, became a flame of fire, and departed. When the king got up early, he ordered gods of gold to be made for him in place of the stone ones, just as the devil had said.
When the king got up early, he ordered gods of gold to be made for him in place of the stone ones, just as the devil had said.
And he had the holy Elijah brought to him.

The king said to him, “What will you say to me now? Can you still tell me that they are not gods? Look, I have made them out of gold. So obey me. Come and worship them before I torture you. [?] I will not spare you another single day.”
The holy Elijah said to the king, “Whatever [?] you want, do it to me quickly.”
For I will not abandon my Lord Jesus Christ and worship things made by human hands.
When the king heard this, he became very angry. He ordered them to split open his toes and pull out their bones.
The king said to him, “Elijah, you have seen how terrible the beginning of the tortures is. So obey me and escape this terrible torture.”
The saint said to him, “I do not care about your tortures, you son of the devil.”
When the king heard this, he became very angry. He ordered them to pull out his fingernails and toenails one by one.
The king said to him, “Obey me so that you may escape terrible tortures. Offer sacrifice, and I will release you.”
The holy Elijah said, “You have now done me a good deed, O king.”
“For it is written like this: ‘Death, where is your sting?’ And the sting of death is sin.”
When the king realized that he had not suffered under this further torture,
he ordered them to strip the skin from his lips and pull out his sinews one by one.
These are the tortures they inflicted on him that day.
The king said, “Elijah, there is just one more torture that I will inflict on you if you do not offer sacrifice. By the life of my kingdom, I will kill you with a terrible death.”
Saint Elijah said to him, “It is written: ‘Do not fear those who kill your body but have no power to destroy your soul.’” When the king heard these things, he ordered them to put him on an iron bed.
These things

And they poured pitch over his body. But he felt nothing under this further harsh torture. Instead, he recited this psalm, saying, “The holy ones will glory in splendor and honor. They will rejoice on their beds. The praises of God are in their throats, and double-edged swords are in their hands.”
He recited this psalm, saying, “The holy ones will glory in splendor and honor. They will rejoice on their beds. The praises of God are in their throats, and double-edged swords are in their hands.”
When the king saw that he had felt nothing under this other torture,
Immediately the king rose from the judgment seat and went to the sea.
He had the holy Elijah brought to him, along with two very fierce wild beasts: a tiger.

And a pregnant lioness. The king ordered them to bring him a small boat made from a log. He had them remove all its ribs and put Saint Elias aboard it with the other wild animals. He had it taken to the middle of the open sea, with him tied beneath the log. They cut the boat’s ropes and left it to be battered by the storm in the middle of the open sea, with Saint Elias aboard it along with the other wild animals.
He turned his face toward the east and prayed as follows, saying, “I beg you, Jesus, Son of the living God, you who saved Daniel from the mouths of the lions:
save me too from these wild animals.
You are the one who saved Jonah, a prophet, while he was inside the sea monster.
Save me too in the middle of this violent sea.”
While Saint Elijah was still praying, he saw that the wild beasts too had turned their faces toward the wall and were crying out to God in their own language.

The righteous man turned again and prayed, saying, “You who led the way before Joseph, guide me too, together with these two irrational animals, through these waves. For just as they have led me astray, they have also led them astray. And look, they are giving glory to your holy name.”
At that very moment Michael and Gabriel came down from heaven. They went to him, greeted him, and said to him, “Be strong, Saint Elias. No one will be able to harm you.
For we have been sent to you to steer your boat until we bring you to the region of Kounthia, because a great struggle awaits you there.”
While the angels were speaking with him, one was sitting at the front of the boat,
and the other at its rear. Immediately they reached the borders of Kounthia.
And the angels of the Lord greeted him, and they went up to heaven in glory and in the peace of God. Amen.
This is the first martyrdom of Saint Elias, which he underwent under Herodianus, king of Thentike. In peace. 99.
Liberianus, the king of Kounthia, went out to the sea and looked out over it. He saw the little boat tossing on the sea,
with Saint Elias aboard it and the wild animals licking his feet. The king immediately ordered
that they bring him in to the shore.
He saw Saint Elias, whose face was radiant with joy. The king said to him, “What country do you belong to? Where are you from?”
The saint said to him, “I am a man of Thentike, and I belong to Jesus Christ.”
When King Liberianus heard the name of Jesus, he stopped short, for he too was an idol worshiper.
He said, “You really are one of those Christian sorcerers!
Indeed, the signs of your sorcery expose you. If you were not a sorcerer, you would not have been saved from these fierce wild animals.
But I am the one who will torture you for your sorcery.”

The devil had stirred up his heart to inflict great evils on the saint. The king ordered them to bind him with iron chains and throw him into a bronze cage until the following day, when he would question him.
He also had the wild animals taken to his menagerie.
Early the next morning, the king ordered them to bring Saint Elias to him in the city’s theater, so that he could question him publicly.
And when the king first [?] him, the king asked him, “What is your name?” The saint said to him, “My name in this world is Elias. My name in the Spirit is ‘The one called by Jesus Christ.’”
The king said to him, “So you have two names, unlike everyone else?”
The saint said to him, “I am not the only one who has two names. Rather, all who believe in my God change their strength

and receive a name according to the Spirit. For those born of the flesh are flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit. Therefore, the name according to the flesh is one thing, and the name according to the Spirit is another.”
When the king heard this, he said, “Elijah, these words will not benefit you at all. You will die horribly.”
And no one will be able to rescue you from my hands.
Saint Elijah said to him, “I would rather die at your hands
than disobey Jesus my God.”
When the king heard these things,

he ordered them to scrape his lips and toes with iron hooks. While they were scraping him, the king shouted to him, “Obey me and offer sacrifice, so that you may be rescued from these great tortures.”
But the saint did not speak at all; instead, he looked up to heaven.
When the king saw that he felt nothing, he ordered them to throw him into a cauldron full of boiling oil and to keep a fire burning beneath it for two hours,
so that his body would be thoroughly scorched. Afterward, they poured resin and pitch over him,
and their flame rose seven cubits above his body.
The king thought that he had already died.
Then he shouted, “Elijah, where is Jesus your God now? Let him rescue you from my hands!”

But the saint was filled with the Holy Spirit. While he was [?] in the fire, he shouted, “Shut your mouth and be silent, lawless king! You are uttering the name of my God with your defiled mouth!” When the king heard that he had not died, he was utterly amazed
and struck his hands together.
He said, “Truly, I have realized what I must do to you to undo your magic. I will send for a magician better than you, so that he may undo your magic,

and I will punish you.” He had them throw him into a chamber, hang him up by his ankles, and lower his head into a jar full of vinegar and lime, with the lime reaching his chest. He sealed the door with his seal until he could send for the magician, bring him, and have them put him to the test against him.
When the king went outside the place where Saint Elijah was confined [?],
Michael the archangel came to Saint Elijah. He lowered him from where he was hanging and sealed his body, and he became as though nothing had touched him at all.
He also brought him some fruit from the trees of paradise for him to eat.
For he had not eaten since the day they put him out to sea with the wild beasts.
Michael said to him, “Be strong, Saint Elijah, victorious runner, crown-winning judge of the contest, our fellow heir with Jesus Christ!
Truly, I tell you, they have already prepared your
throne in the seventh heaven, at Christ’s right hand. Do not be afraid. I will stay with you and help you everywhere they take you.”
After the angel of the Lord had said these things to him, he went up to heaven in glory.
The king sent for a great master magician named Theocletus, who was famous throughout the whole region of Cunthia. When he came to him,
the king said to him, “Theocletus, I have heard of your reputation, that you are a master magician.
Now, then, let your skill be demonstrated against this Christian.
For I have heard that they have a god called Jesus, and whenever they invoke his name, he helps them in every difficulty.”
When Theocletus the magician heard this, he laughed and said to the king, “Do not let these words trouble you. I will show you that I have the power to undo the Christians’ magic.”
The magician got up and [?] the king outside the palace.
They went into a tomb.
He turned his face toward the west.
He invoked the ruler of Tartarus, saying, “Send me a soul so that it may tell the king that I am capable of undoing the Christians’ magic.”
Immediately the ruler of Tartarus came up with a multitude of souls who were bound and being tortured. The magician asked the ruler of Tartarus to open the mouth of one soul and let it speak.

When the soul was allowed to speak, it cried out, saying, “Woe to you, King Liberianus! Woe to everyone who denies this name, Jesus! And you too, Theocletus the magician, are not capable of contending with Elijah the Christian.

Nevertheless, blessed are you, because you will be saved through him, and you will receive what the meaning of your name expresses: ‘the one whom God has saved.’ You will try to harm Elijah, but he will do good to you. You will try to kill him, but he will give you life. Yet I adjure you by the grace that will come upon you: when you receive life through Saint Elijah, remember me too before him.

Perhaps he will plead with his God, Jesus, and he will ease some of the punishments we are suffering. For we are being tortured all the more because we denied him in our ignorance when we were in the world.
Now we understand that Jesus is a merciful God. He forgives the sins of everyone who turns to him with an upright heart.”

When the king heard these words, he said, “What shall we do to Elijah the Christian? He has made the demons appear in an illusion and speak these lies so that we will be afraid and spare him.” The magician answered the king, “Do not think that the words this soul has spoken to us are lies.

Since this soul said, ‘You are not capable of contending with Elijah the Christian, because his God fights on his behalf,’ I believe that the statement is true. For I once heard about ancient magicians who were Egyptians, two brothers, one called Jannes
and the other called Jambres. They opposed a man called Moses,
and they could not overcome him,
because his God fought on his behalf.
Now, then, we too, O king, are going astray in our foolishness, for no one can overcome anyone on whose behalf God fights.
Nevertheless, I do not want to upset you, O king. I will put Elijah the Christian to the test three times. If I cannot overcome him, then truly no one can overcome him.”
The king went into the chamber where the saint was shut up. He found that the seal he had applied was still intact, just as it had been.
The king was saying, “Perhaps you will find him already dead from the torture to which I subjected him.”
When he opened the door and went inside, he smelled a strong, pleasant fragrance in the room. He looked and saw Saint Elijah standing in prayer, with great glory surrounding him.
When the king saw this, he was amazed. At the same time, however, the devils were leading his heart astray,
and he ordered Saint Elijah to be brought out. The magician said,
to the king, “Let us take this Christian
up onto the mountain, away from these crowds, and let the two of us test each other.”
And the king [?] went up onto the mountain with the magician and the saint.
The king said to him, “Elijah, I brought you onto this mountain to test you today.” The saint said to him, “I do not know what magic is, but the power of Jesus my God cannot be overcome.”
The king turned to the magician and said to him, “Whatever you are going to do, do it quickly.”
The magician stood up and uttered an invocation. The mountain split in two.
And two great dragons came up, exceedingly fierce. But Saint Elijah did not look at them at all; he stood praying to God.
When the dragons saw Saint Elijah praying, they stopped,
and they stood still. Fear did not allow them to approach him. When the magician saw this, he was utterly amazed. He labored at his invocations, but the dragons did not move from their place.
The magician wanted to please the king. He said, “Elijah, do you think that you have restrained the dragons
and prevented them from approaching you because my spells have run their course? Look, I tell you: I will do something worse than these things to you.”
Afterward he uttered an invocation, and the dragons split down the middle. He took the dragons’ gall, their [?], and their liver, together with a deadly [?] and a wild [?], and mixed them together.
He put them into a new cup and invoked demonic names over them,
so that the abyss would split open, the devil would come up, and the whole mountain would be filled with demons and apparitions.
When the king saw this, he was exceedingly happy,

and he took hold of the magician’s head and kissed it, saying, “Truly, I have realized that you are capable of undoing the magic of the Christians.” The magician mixed the impure substances together, put them in the cup, and held them out to the righteous man. When he took it, he said, “I did not want to drink any of these impure substances,

but it does not concern me, for it is written in Scripture, ‘Even if they drink a deadly poison, it will not harm them.’ Then Saint Elijah looked up to heaven and prayed, saying, “Hear me, my Lord Jesus Christ, who hears everyone who cries out to him, who heard Abraham during his life as a stranger
and rescued Isaac from the hands of the Philistines;
who rescued Jacob from the hands of Esau; who rescued Joseph from the hand of Potiphar’s wife;
who rescued Moses from the hands of Pharaoh
and from the hands of Jannes and Jambres.
I too, your servant Elijah, beg you to rescue me from the power of these apparitions. Do not let them overcome me, so that the enemy will not boast over me.
For I have heard in the Holy Scripture, ‘If God fights for us, who can oppose us?’ And again Elisha says, ‘Those who fight for us are more numerous than those who oppose us.’

Now, therefore, my Lord Jesus Christ, who rescued Elisha from the hand of the king of Syria, rescue me too from the power of these demons.” When the blessed Elijah finished his plea, Michael the archangel came to him, scourged all the demons, and cast them out of the mountain.
And the other devil became a flame of fire and fled. But the king did not see the angel; only Saint Elias did.
When Saint Elias saw the angel standing beside him, he rejoiced greatly and made the sign of the cross over himself in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.
And he drank the cup full of impurity, and no harm came to him.
Instead, his face was cheerful, like someone filled with wine.
When Publianus saw that Saint Elias had suffered no harm,
he raised his hands and cried out, saying, “Truly, there is no god in heaven or on earth as powerful as Jesus Christ, the God of Saint Elias!”
The magician replied, saying, “There is just one more thing with which I will test you.”
So if no harm has come to you, then your God is truly real.
Immediately the magician uttered an invocation, and a great rock of fire rose from the mountain before them.
He said to the righteous man, “If you trust your God with all your heart, believing that Jesus is a powerful God, then come and enter this rock of fire.
And if no harm comes to you, then I too will believe in your God.”
Saint Elias lifted his eyes to heaven and prayed, saying, “I implore you, Jesus, for whom nothing is impossible.

I implore you, Jesus, the hope of those who trust in him. I implore you, Jesus, the pride of the righteous, the crown of the martyrs. You are the one who said in the holy Scriptures, ‘No fire will harm you.’
Again you said, ‘Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.’ Therefore I trust that you have power over all things.

You who saved the three saints from the blazing, fiery furnace, save me too, so that your glory may be revealed before this magician and Publianus the senator.” Immediately a cloud of dew came from heaven and covered the saint’s body like a garment.
And he made the sign of the cross over himself and entered the fire.
He spent two hours in the midst of the fire, praying. Afterward he came out of the fire.
No harm at all had come to him, and there was not even the smell of fire on his clothes.
The magician and the senator approached him and greeted him, saying, “Truly, your God Jesus is a true God,
and nothing is impossible for him. We implore you, O Saint Elias, to ask your God to grant us the crown of being Christians.”

Saint Elias rejoiced greatly, stretched out his hands, and prayed, saying, “I implore you, my Lord Jesus Christ, the forgiving God: forgive Theocletus the magician and Publianus the senator. You yourself said, ‘I do not desire the sinner’s death, but rather that he turn back and repent.’
Again you said, ‘I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.’
Now, therefore, I implore you to transform this rock of fire into a spring of water, so that I may baptize those you have chosen in your holy name,
and they may receive the seal of life. You yourself said to your disciples, ‘Go out into the whole world and baptize all nations in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.’”
And at that very moment,
the rock of fire was transformed.
It became a spring of flowing water.
And Saint Elijah baptized Theocletus the magician and Publianus the senator.
And he sealed them in the name of the Father and the Son,
and the Holy Spirit, for the forgiveness of their sins.
When the king saw this, he became extremely angry because the magician and the senator had believed in the Lord Jesus. He came down from that mountain.
He ordered the magician and the senator to be beheaded together.
The senator Publianus had three friends, who came to visit him while he was bound.

They said to him, “What has happened to you, our friend? Is the king holding you over some money that you have been unable to find and pay? If so, we will give you whatever the king is holding you for.” He said to them, “If you are willing to listen to me, do what I, your friend, tell you.”

“I ask nothing of you except that you acknowledge the God of Saint Elijah, so that you may receive the crown that never perishes.” Immediately they cried out, “We are ready to die for his holy name!” They all cried out to the king, “We are Christians!” Publius the senator was there with his three friends, his troop of soldiers, the members of their households, and Theocletus the magician as well. The king ordered pits to be dug and filled with fire, and the saints to be thrown into them.

And he burned them all in a single day. This is how Publius the senator, Theocletus the magician, and everyone with him completed their martyrdom, numbering nine hundred and seventy-four. On the twentieth of Meshir they went up to heaven in glory.
After this, they brought Saint Elijah before the tribunal.
The king said to him, “Elijah, do you think that because you have killed my magician, I will be afraid of you and release you?”
“By the power of my kingship,
I will torture you cruelly until I see whether Jesus can rescue you from my hands.”
But Saint Elijah remained silent and did not speak at all.
Instead, he looked up to heaven.
The king ordered them to insert skewers:
two red-hot ones into his ears and another two into his eyes.
After that, they were to pull out his tongue,
so that his brain would burn. Afterward, he ordered them to put him on a bed
of iron and pour boiling lead over him.
But Saint Elijah endured this further torture with
steadfastness.
Afterward, he had them strip the skin from his head and put a helmet on him.

And the saint endured this further torture. Afterward, he ordered them to dig a pit in the ground matching his length and breadth, and had them lower the saint into it. Then he had them light a fire beneath a cauldron filled with lead until it became like water, turn the apparatus, and pour it down over his body until it reached his neck. Immediately Michael the archangel stood over him. He did not let the fire or the boiling lead touch him at all; instead, it was like cool water to him.
When the king saw that it did not trouble him, he became very angry.
The king stood up, took his sword himself, and with his own hand slit the righteous man’s belly. His intestines fell down onto the ground.
Immediately, a cloud of light overshadowed him. The angel of the Lord took his intestines and put them back into his belly as before,
and healed his whole body. He became as though they had not touched him at all.
But when the king saw that he had been unable to overcome him:

He said, “I know what I will do. I will send him to Eutychodorus. Perhaps he has a very powerful magician with him.” He rose from the tribunal and ordered that he be confined until he had written his report.
He took a sheet of papyrus and wrote on it as follows: “I, Liberianus, king of Cunthia, write to Eutychodorus, king of the Medes. Greetings.
“Since the Christians have rebelled through acts of magic, they deserve death.
“Look, I have sent you one of them, whose name is Elijah, so that you may kill him.”
Then he ordered that Saint Elijah be brought out and handed over to two guards. They boarded a sailing vessel on the sea. They bound Saint Elijah and threw him into the hold of the ship.
When they had set sail, Michael came down from heaven with a cloud of light. He went down into the hold of the ship, untied Saint Elijah, and lifted him onto the cloud of light.
He took him up to the heavens.
He saw all the saints and greeted them, and they encouraged him. He took him up to the third heaven,
and also to paradise, with the tree of life in its midst.
Then he took him into the land of the inheritance.
He saw it: its ground was white like fine silver, and it abounded in trees laden with very good fruit.
Then they took him to the city of Christ.
Twelve walls surrounded that city.
Then they showed him a great house like a royal palace, built inside the wall. Its area was sixteen arouras. It was built entirely of gold and pearls, and its height was a thousand cubits.
Its roof was built of precious stones and shone more brightly than the sun.

Michael said to him, “Saint Elijah, this house built of gold and pearls is yours.” When Saint Elijah heard these words, he rejoiced greatly. As he was walking through the city, the Lord Jesus came from heaven before him.
He said to him, “Be strong, Elijah, my beloved. Your contest has drawn near. Look, you have seen how many good things are prepared for those who will believe in me with all their heart.

“I am Jesus, the good news of all the ages. Look, today I bring good news to you too. But you, my beloved, when they take you to Media, Eutychodorus, king of Media, will kill you, for you will complete your contest at his hands.”
Saint Elijah answered and said to the Savior, “My Lord, I do not want to remain among the godless nations, lest they scatter my bones and wipe out my memory from the earth.”

The Savior said to him, “Truly I tell you, my chosen Elijah, just as the dew of heaven spreads over the whole earth, so they will glorify my name through you because of the miracles that will take place through your body.
“And because you have asked me to have your body taken away from the nations, I will put your heart at ease and fulfill your request.
“After some days, I will reveal your memorial in a dream to righteous people living in Egypt. I will have them come for your body, take it up to Egypt, and lay it there.
“And in the place where they will lay your body, I will have them lay the bodies of other righteous people—
“two of them—in it.
“And the place where they will lay your body will be a temple for me forever.”
And everyone who comes into your sanctuary and asks me for anything in faith, in your name, I will do it for him.
And all people suffering from any illness, if they come into your sanctuary and appeal to you in your name, I will grant them [?]. I will make your healing
name famous everywhere, and I will cause great miracles and wonders to take place in your burial place.
But when the Lord Jesus sent these up to heaven in glory,
And immediately the ship docked at the harbor of Media, the metropolis of Nemetos.
And the guards gave the letters to King Eutychodorus.
THE SECOND MARTYRDOM OF SAINT ELIJAH, WHICH HE UNDERWENT UNDER LIBERIANUS, KING OF CUNTHIA. IN PEACE. AMEN.

When they gave the report concerning Saint Elijah to Eutychodorus, king of Media, he read everything they had written about him. He had him confined until the next day, when he would hear his case. He wrote a reply to the letters and sent them
to be taken to their king in their country. The next day the king sat on the judgment seat and had Saint Elijah brought to him.

The king said to him, “Elijah, what are these evil deeds that they have written to me saying you do? Now, then, offer sacrifice.” The righteous man answered, “It is written in the holy Scriptures: ‘You shall not worship things made by hands, for I am God, and there is no other
besides me.’” When the king heard these things, he had him hung on a ship’s mast and ordered them to shoot arrows at him for three hours.
But Saint Elijah marked himself with the sign of the cross.
Immediately a cloud of light covered him, and not a single arrow touched him at all.
When the king saw this, he was greatly astonished and ordered them to take him down from the wooden mast.

The king said to him, “Elijah, I want you to explain to me this sign you made on your forehead, so that you were saved from these powerful arrows. I say to myself that what you did was magic; otherwise you would not have survived.” Saint Elijah said to him, “O king, do not think that what I did was magic. Certainly not! Rather, this is the sign of the cross of my Lord Jesus Christ.” The king said to him, “Was your Lord hung up? What did they do to him?”

The righteous man said to him, “He went up onto the cross and died for our sins.” The king said to him, “Then your God also died like everyone else?” The righteous man said, “Indeed, he is immortal, but he died and rose again to give us life.” The king said to him, “Truly, I will kill you too by the death that your God Jesus died.”
Then he ordered them to make a cross and hang the saint on it. When they raised the saint onto it, he rejoiced because he had been found worthy of the Lord’s likeness.
And immediately a dove of light settled on the right arm of the cross,
and another on the left arm. They spread their wings over him and covered him, because he was naked.
And a voice reached him, saying, “O Elijah, here is the form that I bore, I, the Son of God. Look, you too have borne it.
For they hung me on the cross and placed me between two robbers. Truly I tell you, my chosen Elijah, the form you have borne is indeed exalted.”
And when Jesus finished speaking with him, cherubim and [?] appeared. A great fear
fell upon everyone around him.
And the angels came, released the saint, and took him down from the cross. They carried away the cross and hurried away, leaving Saint Elijah standing.

When the king saw these things, he was amazed. He rose from the judgment seat that day and had him confined until the next day. The next day, when the king became extremely angry because the devil had filled his heart with every [?] against him, he immediately sat on the judgment seat and ordered the saint to be brought to him. The king said to him, “Elijah, do you think that you can practice magical arts so that you survive on [?], since there is no more torture for you?” The king ordered them to break the joints of his hands and those of his feet.
And he was threatening him.
And he ordered them to strike his head with an iron hammer until his brains came out through his mouth and nose.
When the king saw that he had not been burned by all these things he had done to him,
he had some very fierce wild animals brought to him: a leopard and a male wild boar.
He had Saint Elijah thrown to them, thinking that they would tear him apart immediately.

When the wild animals saw Saint Elijah praying to God, they ran up to him, wagging their tails at him, and bowed down and paid homage to him. The king was greatly astonished and realized that he could not overcome him. He passed sentence on him, ordering that he be beheaded, taken to an island in the sea, and left there. As Saint Elijah was about to be taken out to be beheaded, he turned his face eastward and prayed as follows, saying, “I bless you, my Lord Jesus Christ, because I have been found worthy to reach this hour and die for your holy name. I beg you, my Lord, do not put me to shame when I come before you.”
Immediately the sweet voice of the Lord reached him: “Truly I tell you, my chosen Elijah, my Father’s heart is satisfied with your struggle.
Look, [?] in heaven have put on crowns before you. Conquer, you who have conquered! Be strong, you who have been strong!”
When Saint Elijah heard these things, he sealed himself in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
He stretched out his neck, and they cut off his head at the ninth hour on the sixteenth day of Parmhat.
The angels and all the saints came out to meet him and greeted him,
and they sang the song of Alleluia until they brought him to the city of Christ.
After they had cut off his head, they took his body and left it on an island in the middle of the sea,

until the day when God revealed him in a vision to two righteous monks in the land of Egypt, so that they would go and get his body, bring it to Egypt, and place it in the place the Lord had prepared for him. This is how he completed his martyrdom. He went up to heaven in glory and received the imperishable crown in peace. Amen.

All those who were martyred with Saint Elijah received the crown of eternal life. They numbered six thousand four hundred and thirty souls. Together with Saint Elijah, they entered into life. May their holy blessing be with us. Amen.
This is how Saint Elijah completed his honored struggle on the sixteenth day of Parmhat, having fallen into the hands of three kings, who were these:
Herodian, the king of the Indians—and Saint Elijah was a native of that country.
The second was Liberian, the king of Kunthia. The third was Eutychodorus, the king of Nemethos. Under him Elijah completed his struggle and went up to heaven in glory and honor.
May we too come to enjoy the good things of the kingdom of heaven through the grace
and the love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ. To him be glory, together with his good Father and the life-giving and consubstantial Holy Spirit, now and at all times, forever and ever. Amen.
